previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of acute on chronic systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, paroxysmal ventricular tachycardia, coronary atherosclerosis, type 2 diabetes, and stage 3B chronic kidney disease, was admitted for worsening dyspnea, orthopnea, and lower extremity edema due to fluid overload. The exacerbation was triggered by missing multiple heart failure medications, including amiodarone, spironolactone, digoxin, and metoprolol, and dietary indiscretions. He was treated with IV furosemide initially, then transitioned to oral torsemide with a one-time metolazone boost. His weight decreased from 137.4 kg to 129.2 kg, near his known dry weight. He had a transient rise in creatinine to 2.7, consistent with cardiorenal physiology, and was evaluated by nephrology who confirmed stage 3B CKD without need for dialysis. A positive urinalysis was treated briefly with ceftriaxone, but culture was negative. He remained on home medications for heart failure and arrhythmia, with spironolactone resumed after potassium normalized. He was enrolled in the PACT program for outpatient support and discharged home with close follow-up in cardiology and nephrology.

#Chest pain
Patient was evaluated for ACS; there were some non-specific EKG 
changes; his troponin was slightly elevated at 0.03 but remained 
stable for 3 measurements, and his chest pressure resolved with 
diuresis.

#Acute on chronic systolic congestive Heart failure exacerbation
Patient was significantly volume overloaded on presentation. He 
stated that he was taking all of his medications at home, 
however he also reported eating and drinking large volumes in 
the setting of several recent losses in his family.
Labs on admission were notable for H+H 12.1/38.9 BUN/Creat 
___ trop 0.03 x2 BNP 6042  
During his stay diuresis was attempted with IV Lasix boluses, 
Lasix drip and with PO torsemide. Mr ___ was very reluctant to 
be placed on lasix drip and was very concerned that it causes 
many of his problems, including headache and worsening kidney 
function. He often refused treatment throughout his stay and 
diuresis was repeatedly re-negotiated. We attempted to explain 
that his kidney function was most likely getting worse in the 
setting of heart failure due to insufficient diuresis, but the 
patient was not convinced.
Other adjustments in his medication included increasing his 
hydralazine from 30mg TID to 40mg TID, and increasing his 
isosorbide XL from 60mg daily to 90 mg daily. His spironolactone 
was stopped in the setting of rising creatinine and concerns for 
worsening kidney function.
On the day of discharge he informed the team that he would 
prefer to be treated outpatient in the heart failure clinic and 
would not allow any more IV diuresis. He was discharged on his 
home dose of torsemide (80mg BID), 

#Chronic Kidney Disease
Baseline creatinine is 1.7-2.1. History of diabetes melltius and 
 hypertension.
Creatinine was 1.8 on admission. Cr stayed around 2.0 early in 
his stay when he was still agreeing to a lasix drip. As he 
decreased his diuresis later in the admission, creatinine 
increased to 2.5. CKD was likely exacerbated in setting of 
decompensated CHF causing cardiorenal syndrome.

# H/o VT and atrial fibrillation:  
 Patient has ICD in place.  Continued home Amiodarone and 
digoxin .
